svg.title: Outlook connector code map
svg.desc: The connector's main classes and who calls whom. The command line starts the MCP server or the web UI, prepares sign-in, or shows its status. Both surfaces call service classes: Mailbox, Conversations, Exports, Files, Writes, Mutations, Calendar, CalendarListing, Rules and Signatures. The service depends on the ports in remote/ports.py: MailReader, MailWriter, RuleWriter, SignatureStore and four calendar ports. Graph adapters (GraphMailReader, GraphCalendarView) and Outlook Web adapters (OwsMailWriter, OwsRules, OwsCalendarItems, OwsCalendarWindow, SubstrateEventSearch, CloudSettings) implement them; every remote request shares one Transport and the shared TokenProvider. Mailbox keeps only the folder cache and account binding in the local Store. AppContext in bootstrap.py builds the services once per process. Hover an item for details.
svg.text: Main classes and who calls whom · arrows point to the callee · hover an item for details
__main__.py · main() parses the command, then calls its handler by name (match)

g.title: Builds the FastMCP server around one AppContext and runs it over stdio until the client closes it.
Starts uvicorn on 127.0.0.1 with a per-run session token, opens the browser, and stops after the idle timeout.
The only place that ever prompts: prepares every shared profile silently where it can, and shows a device code only for profiles that need one.
With --sign-out: deletes the shared token cache (every profile, every connector).
Offline view of the cache: no network calls, no token values.
With --check only: silent acquisition per profile; not a service-permission test.
Mail folders with paths (e.g. Inbox/Projects/Project Alpha), well-known aliases and counts. → Mailbox.folders
Messages newest first, from the server; folder optional (whole mailbox), date window, scope, cursor. → Mailbox.list_messages
Server-side search of mail only; hits grouped by conversation in rank order, with each conversation's message_count. → Mailbox.search
A whole conversation across folders, oldest first; body=unique strips quoted history. → Conversations.get_conversation
One message's body (full/unique/html) with offset continuation, plus attachment metadata. → Mailbox.get_message
Attachment metadata; kind=item is a forwarded email, kind=reference a cloud link. → Mailbox.attachments
Save one attachment as a local file and return its path (forwarded emails as .eml). → Files.download_attachment
Save the original message (MIME) as a local .eml file and return its path. → Files.save_mime
Export conversations, messages and/or a folder or date window to one local file (TXT or JSONL, optional attachments); returns its path. → Exports.export
Offline sign-in status: the bound account and each profile's cached credential. → TokenProvider.status
Exchange events by words through Search v2, one bounded page at a time. → Calendar.search_events
Events overlapping a window, in time order, Graph first. → CalendarListing.list_events
One event's agenda, attendees, join URL and attachment metadata. → Calendar.get_event
Save explicit text or HTML into Drafts; require Graph read-back. → Writes.create_draft
Send the existing server draft unchanged, once, after human approval. → Writes.send_draft
Mark messages (or whole conversations) read or unread; read receipts are never sent. → Mutations.set_read
Flag or unflag messages. A result per message. → Mutations.set_flag
Move messages to a folder (not Deleted Items). A result per message. → Mutations.move
Move messages to Deleted Items; never a permanent delete. → Mutations.delete
Rules in priority order; unsupported rules are read-only. → Rules.list_rules
Without a code: a proposal. With the user's code: one write, read back. → Rules.create_rule
Partial edits; enabling or disabling is its own update. → Rules.update_rule
The full order of supported rules; refused while unsupported rules exist. → Rules.reorder_rules
Delete one supported rule after confirmation. → Rules.delete_rule
Native signature names and the new-mail and reply defaults. → Signatures.list_signatures
One signature's HTML and text. → Signatures.get_signature
Create from passive HTML; one write, resent only when Outlook refused it as throttled or unavailable (429, 503). → Signatures.create_signature
Replace contents from passive HTML; does not rename. → Signatures.update_signature
Delete one signature; a selected default may be left dangling. → Signatures.delete_signature
Set or clear the new-mail and/or reply default. → Signatures.set_default_signature

svg.text: surfaces/web/web_main.py serve_ui() · routes.py: Starlette JSON API + static JS

g.title: GET. The folder tree for the sidebar (?refresh=1 reloads it). → Mailbox.folders
GET. One page of a folder, newest first, with the scope switches and a cursor. → Mailbox.list_messages
GET. One message's body for the reading pane. → Mailbox.get_message
GET. Server-side search, grouped by conversation. → Mailbox.search
GET. The whole conversation with bodies. → Conversations.get_conversation
POST. Message counts for the listed conversations (the row badges). → Mailbox.conversation_sizes
GET. Download one attachment. → Files.download_attachment
POST. Attachment names for many messages at once (the file chips on rows). → Mailbox.attachments_many
POST. Export the selection to one file and download it. → Exports.export
GET. Offline sign-in status and the sign-in command to show. → TokenProvider.status
GET. Your name and address for the header. → Mailbox.profile
GET. Your profile photo, or nothing when none is set. → Mailbox.photo
POST. Keeps the idle timer from stopping the UI while the page is open.

service/ · every domain decision; validates input once at the entry point; never sees HTTP, MCP, Graph or OWS JSON

g.title: The visible folders. Cached in the Store and used only while younger than 10 minutes; otherwise the call waits for a refresh.
A folder id, a well-known alias (inbox, archive, ...), a path (Inbox/Projects) or a name. Hidden folders are refused.
Folder id → reason for every folder the scope leaves out (Deleted Items/Junk, Sent/Drafts/Outbox).
The folder map and the ids of hidden folders (out of reach for lists and search).
Newest first. Without a folder: whole mailbox, or folder by folder when left-out folders hold ≥ 66% of the mailbox. Copies merged, meeting mail optional, cursor.
Server-side $search, hits grouped by conversation, ids translated to immutable ids.
One message's body with offset continuation, and its attachment metadata.
Attachment metadata of one message, or of many at once (batched).
How many messages each conversation has, counted the way get_conversation lists them.
A whole conversation across folders, oldest first, with bounded bodies and a cursor. Bodies that could not be fetched carry an ExportError block.
All messages of the conversation, oldest first, what was left out by folder, and whether the server listing was truncated.
Text bodies from the server, in $batch requests of 20.

svg.text: copies of a message shown once (also_in)

g.title: Export a selection (conversations, messages, a folder or date window) to one local file: TXT for people or JSONL for agents, a ZIP when there are several files or attachments.
formatter.py renders TXT/JSONL; attachments.py is the selection policy and safe file names; packaging.py builds the one output file.
Save one attachment as a local file (forwarded emails as .eml) and return its path.
Save the original message (MIME) as a local .eml named after its subject.

svg.text: files kept a week under the data folder

g.title: Save explicit text or HTML (checked once by passive_html) into Drafts with the native signature; require Graph read-back. Replies are checked for intact quoted history. Nothing is sent.

Send an existing draft exactly as stored, once, bound to the change key it was read at. An unclear answer is checked against Sent Items and never resent; the send is resent only when Outlook refused it as throttled or unavailable (429, 503).
Refuses to write unless the Outlook sign-in is the bound Microsoft account.
Mark messages, and every message of the given conversations in scope, read or unread.
Flag or unflag messages.
Move to a folder (not Deleted Items, not a hidden folder).
Move to Deleted Items; messages already there are left alone. Never a hard delete.
Exchange events by words through Search v2, across all dates; one bounded page and a cursor.
One event read through Outlook Web GetItem: agenda verbatim, attendees, join URL, attachment metadata.

svg.text: no totals; no cursor at offset 1,000

g.title: Events overlapping a window, in time order, recurring meetings expanded, times in UTC; optional contains and descriptions.

svg.text: Graph first; Outlook Web only when a
a cursor keeps the service that answered

g.title: Every inbox rule in priority order; unsupported fields make a rule read-only.
Each change first returns a proposal and a code bound to the account and every current rule revision.
With the user's code: one OWS write, resent only when Outlook refused it as throttled or unavailable (429, 503), then a fresh read-back.

svg.text: propose → confirm → one write → read back

g.title: Names, defaults and contents, read fresh; each content read must share the account scope.
Passive HTML (checked by passive_html) plus quoted data-URI images; each write is resent only when Outlook refused it as throttled or unavailable (429, 503).
New-mail and reply defaults, set or cleared independently.
The signature block create_draft appends: the default for new mail or replies, or a named one; images become inline attachments.
Self-contained continuation cursors: everything needed to continue travels in the cursor (processes are short-lived).
One classification of failed Microsoft requests: ExportError (step, status, code, likely cause, retry, fix).
Output folders under the data directory; files older than a week are removed; exclusive file creation.
Validation shared by the entry points that accept mailbox scope.
Concurrent reads that finish or are cancelled before their caller returns.
The one HTML check for draft bodies and signatures: no active content, no markup left open, no elements that change how the rest is read.
Pydantic models: the single schema for the service, the MCP tools and the web API. Never mirrors a Microsoft wire format.
ConnectorError and its kinds (NotFound, Throttled, AuthenticationRequired, WriteOutcomeUnknown, ...); surfaces know how to present them.
A time without a zone is UTC; an aware time is converted. Applied once where a window enters.

svg.text: validate once, at the entry point

g.title: The cached folders and their age in seconds (None when never cached). Mailbox uses them only while younger than 10 minutes.
Replace the cached folder list (one short transaction).
The folder list with paths, counts and hidden flags.
Which account owns this store; another account's store is left untouched and a separate one is used.

svg.text: remote/ · ports in ports.py, one adapter per port; the only code that knows wire formats and ids

g.title: Every folder, hidden ones included (the service decides what is out of reach).
One page of messages, newest first; a continuation, or skip N.
One page of $search hits.
Every message of a conversation in every folder, and whether it was truncated.
Server count per folder in a window ($count in one $batch).
One message, or many in batches; per-item failures are reported, not raised.
Batch lookup of summaries (folder, read state, flag).
Attachment metadata per message.
An attachment, or the message's MIME, streamed to a file.
The signed-in user's name, address and photo.
One page of the default calendar's events in a window, occurrences expanded, times in UTC.
Save into Drafts without sending; the draft's id when the backend reports it.
Send an existing draft as it is, keeping a copy in Sent Items. Raises WriteOutcomeUnknown when it cannot tell.
Identity claims (tid, oid, upn) of the Outlook credential.
Read or unread; one outcome per message.
Move to a folder, or to Deleted Items; there is no hard delete.
Inbox rules: list, create, update, reorder and delete.
Native signature settings and contents: read, create, update, delete, set defaults.
Hydrate one event by its Outlook item id.
The calendar window without descriptions, for when the Graph read fails.
One page of Exchange event hits from Search v2.
Builds Graph URLs and query options; graph_mapping.py converts every Graph shape into domain models.
$search returns regular ids; one translateExchangeIds call per page turns them into the immutable ids every other call uses.
/me/calendarView with UTC times and text bodies, next links followed; ids converted to the Outlook Web form.
Built on its own Graph client with the profile in config.CALENDAR_PROFILE, because the Outlook Graph profile has no calendar scope.
CreateItem (SaveOnly) for drafts and replies; UpdateItem for read, flag and send_draft (SendAndSaveCopy); MoveItem; DeleteItem with MoveToDeletedItems.
Inbox-rule actions in OWS's bare-request style.
GetItem with the default event shape plus body and attachment metadata.
GetCalendarView for the default calendar in UTC; the fallback for a failed Graph read.
Search v2 Event/Exchange pages; Cvid and LogicalId kept across one walk. Calls Transport directly.
Implements SignatureStore over Outlook Cloud Settings. Calls Transport directly.
One JSON request; POST is for read-style APIs (search), so it is retried like a GET.
One page and the link to the next; or follow pages up to a maximum, stopping at a repeated link.
Many GETs in $batch requests of 20, at most 2 in flight; throttled sub-requests re-sent after the advised delay.
A small binary GET (the profile photo).
Stream a file to disk with a size cap.
Every request asks for immutable ids, which survive moves.

call: one item action in the JsonRequest envelope, resent only when Outlook refused it as throttled or unavailable (429, 503). call_read and call_view: reads, retried like GETs (call_view for GetCalendarView, whose items sit directly in Body).
Inbox-rule actions use this bare-request style; success is indicated by WasSuccessful and ErrorCode.
Claims of the Outlook token: the account writes act as.
Send one request with the named profile's token; return a successful response or raise a domain error.
request() and parse the JSON answer (size-capped).
Stream a GET body to a file, size-capped.
Only the configured Microsoft hosts (urls.py); at most 4 concurrent requests per mailbox (Exchange's limit).
Up to 4 attempts, honouring Retry-After. Writes are retried only on 429 or 503 (nothing applied); no answer or another 5xx = WriteOutcomeUnknown, never resent.
A rejected token is refreshed once (with the CAE claims challenge, if any); a second 401 asks for sign-in.

lrh-m365-auth · shared MSAL profiles · no app registration, no secrets

g.title: Silent: memory, then the cache, refreshing if needed. Never prompts. Called by Transport for every request (through AccountBoundTokenSource).
Prepare every profile: silent where possible, a device code only where needed. Only the auth command calls it.
Delete the cache; or an offline view of it (no network, no token values).
Graph Mail.Read for mailbox data and User.Read for the signed-in profile and photo.
→ outlook.office.com. Mail changes, inbox rules, native signatures, event details and the calendar fallback.
→ Search v2, for calendar event search.
Shared with the Teams connector; carries the calendar scope used by the Graph calendar view.
Shared token-cache.bin under .lrh-m365-auth, encrypted for your user by the operating system; a lock file serialises refreshes across processes.
One active Microsoft account is shared by every lrh-* Microsoft 365 connector.

svg.text: Built once per process, on first use

g.title: Encrypted cache unless --unsecure (a separate plaintext development cache).
Every token request is checked against the account the store is bound to.
One HTTPS client for every Microsoft service.
The MailReader adapter.
SQLite file per account fingerprint; everything else reads mail through Mailbox.
SubstrateEventSearch for search, OwsCalendarItems for details.
GraphCalendarView on Graph(transport, profile=CALENDAR_PROFILE), with OwsCalendarWindow as the fallback.
Mail-change and inbox-rule adapters on one Ows client.
Native signatures over Cloud Settings.

svg.text: Each layer calls only the one below it.
The service sees only its ports, so
Graph and Outlook Web stay swappable.
API flows are neutral; one shared Transport.

file directly in a browser (tooltips do
not show when it is embedded as an image).
first-party public clients · no app registration

Event details, and the calendar window when Graph fails.
OWS rule actions support reading and confirmed changes to supported inbox rules.
